items.title: Undefined registers in inline bitboard operations
items.summary: The recovered inline-bitboard caller reproduces all four historical undefined-register errors on a reconstructed fork differing only by absence of existing patch 0028. Identical retained IR passes with 0028, and the recovered probe matches the host oracle on a16 and xy16 in bsnes-jg. The same C input passes supported unpatched-upstream configurations.
items.nextStep: Carry the 0028 root fix with the compiler feature series.

items.title: GlobalISel physical-register inline-asm range exhaustion
items.summary: An i128 AArch64 inline-asm operand constrained to {cc} exhausts the one-register class and asserts. Patch 0056 validates the whole physical-register range, diagnoses invalid constraints, and defines error-recovery results without invoking fallback. The identical IR changes from an assertion to the expected clean diagnostic on the isolated candidate.
items.nextStep: Use independently reviewed 0056 exact-current LLVM packet; post only when requested.

items.title: llvm-reduce crashes reducing MIR with two workers
items.summary: The retained MIR input crashes the preserved llvm-reduce with -j 2; keeping MachineModuleInfo in each parallel MIR work item lets the same input reduce successfully while preserving IR bitcode workers. This is the dated September 25 local candidate result, not an endorsement of general shared-context parallel safety. September 26 reconciliation finds an existing September 24 upstream CLI guard; the ready MOS packet backports that guard instead of proposing another LLVM repair.
items.nextStep: Use exact MOS backport packet, credit upstream b1ba3d515a02, and post only when requested; no new LLVM bug.

items.title: 65816 bank relaxation ignores a section offset above 65535
items.summary: Fixed: an out-of-bank section-relative symbol can relax to long addressing even when its section is not marked far.
items.nextStep: Carry with downstream far-section policy; do not report a pristine-upstream defect.

items.title: Fine-grained carry pressure is lost before register pressure set pruning
items.summary: Patch 0064 models computed Cc values directly in the MOS pre-RA scheduler and removes avoidable carry saves on the recovered sum/rotate inputs: 409 to 248 bytes and 385 to 285 bytes. The generic TableGen fine-grained pressure-set contract remains uncorrected; its broader repair was rejected after corpus regressions. The scheduler mitigation passes matching-input MIR checks and runtime validation. September 27 emulator timing: original sum/rotate use 30.45%/17.61% fewer master clocks, while the isolated XY16 Oz L-system interpreter uses 2.80% more. The zero-cycle-regression criterion is not met. Patch 0067 compares always and gated policies: aggregate savings versus off are 213866 B and 199309 B, with 39 and six growing objects. The gate recovers the 32 original growth cases. The LLVM-facing report presents these trade-offs and selection options without an upstream default decision; the current downstream compiler defaults to always. A subsequent profitability screen tests three pressure-cost models: all give up aggregate savings and increase total positive growth. Complete-object selection is implemented and measured; including gated among off/always alternatives gains 220 B in 55 configurations. A writable-storage cap selects 211974 B of savings, with no selected file/writable-section growth in the frozen census; object selection does not imply per-function or universal speed improvement.
items.nextStep: PR #609 remains withdrawn. The LLVM-facing investigation presents carry-policy measurements and implementation options without selecting a default. Evaluate completed-output size selection and narrower gating, with compile-time and timing coverage. The downstream compiler currently defaults to always; the generic pressure contract and baseline runtime observations remain open.

items.title: 0015 coalescing witness: undefined lane after identity-copy removal
items.summary: The retained rcundef.c witness reproduces the historical undefined-rc3 signature on an identified current fork reconstructed without 0015 and 0028. Adding only existing patch 0028 repairs the same IR; 0015 is a trigger-avoidance workaround for this witness. Rewriter output differs only by three KILL pseudos, with identical register assignments. The existing eight-instruction model reproduces on saved unpatched upstream 742d554 using mos6502; stock C reachability remains unproven.

items.title: Far loads and stores on non-65816 CPUs emit 65816 [dp] opcodes
items.summary: The p2:32:8 data layout applies to every MOS CPU, and the far runtime-address path does not check hasW65816(); selection does not enforce the HasW65816 predicate on LDIndirLong. A runtime far byte load compiles for mos6502 without error and emits $A7 $00, which the 6502 decodes as an undocumented LAX, the SPC700 as sbc a,[$0+x] and the HuC6280 as smb. Far global loads on those CPUs fail loudly; runtime loads and stores do not. Found by the independent review (finding B3) and reproduced on the downstream toolchain.
items.nextStep: Fixed downstream in 0002 on 2026-09-30 (plan docs/plans/2026-09-30-far-prerequisite-defects.md); carry into the split #320 series.

items.title: Opt-in split and A:X+Y far-pointer conventions crash when a far pointer is followed by another argument
items.summary: Under the opt-in +mos-farcc-split or +mos-farcc-axy far-pointer calling convention, a function whose far-pointer argument (assigned by the custom CC_MOS_FarPtrSplit / CC_MOS_FarPtrAXY assigner) is followed by any other argument aborts in CallLowering::handleAssignments during the IRTranslator: two far pointers, or one far pointer then an i8. The release build aborts with no diagnostic (exit 134). The matching call site does not terminate: IRTranslator memory grows until an address-space limit gives "LLVM ERROR: out of memory", or the kernel OOM killer ends llc. A single far-pointer argument compiles, which is all the existing farcc_split/farcc_axy gates exercise. The same holds with +mos-xy16 and on the B1-B4 candidate. The default Imag32 convention and the opt-in Stack convention are not affected. Found while testing the B1 stack fallback against these conventions (plan docs/plans/2026-09-30-far-prerequisite-defects.md, Outcome).
items.nextStep: Root-cause the custom far-pointer value handling in call lowering for the opt-in split and A:X+Y conventions, or retire those variants; the default Imag32 convention is unaffected.

items.title: Far addressing folds other than the runtime-index fold leave dangling DBG_VALUEs
items.summary: Three far addressing-mode folds erase or rewrite an access and leave the G_PTR_ADDs that computed its pointer with only debug uses: the absolute-long fold (tryFarAbsoluteAddressing, #320-2), the [dp],Y displacement window in tryFarIndirectIndexedAddressing (#320-4), and the absolute-long indexed fold (tryFarAbsoluteIndexedAddressing, far-word patch 5 / downstream 0061). The legalizer erases the dead adds; salvageDebugInfoForDbgValue cannot express a G_PTR_ADD and leaves the DBG_VALUE on the erased register, which DetectDeadLanes marks undef, so -g with -verify-machineinstrs fails ("Generic virtual register use cannot be undef"). The simplest -g far field access (base + 1) fails at O0 and O2 on the reviewed split and on the downstream release toolchain. Emitted code is unaffected. This is the mechanism of mos-far-index-fold-dangling-dbg (B4) at the fold sites its repair did not cover.

items.title: Far runtime-index fold leaves an undef DBG_VALUE that fails machine verification
items.summary: When tryFarRuntimeIndexFold folds every non-debug use of a far pointer add into a [dp],Y access, salvageDebugInfo cannot express base + zext(offset) and leaves the DBG_VALUE naming the dead vreg. DetectDeadLanes marks it undef and -verify-machineinstrs rejects the function. Without the verifier the location degrades to $noreg and the emitted code is unaffected. The byte fold (0061/patch 4) and the native word fold (0070) both fail downstream. Found by the independent review (finding B4) and reproduced on the downstream toolchain.
items.nextStep: Fixed downstream in 0002 on 2026-09-30 (plan docs/plans/2026-09-30-far-prerequisite-defects.md); carry into the split #320 series.

items.title: Far memset/memcpy/memmove lengths above 65535 are truncated or deleted
items.summary: createFarMemLibcall truncated the length of an address-space-2 G_MEMSET, G_MEMCPY or G_MEMMOVE to 16 bits without a range check. A constant 70000-byte far memset called __memset_far with 4464, and a runtime i32 memcpy length lost its high 16 bits. The compiler exited 0 and the verifier was clean. The input's len64k function (a 65536-byte memmove from a near pointer, which the IRTranslator narrows to 16 bits and so deletes) is not a defect: LangRef "Allocated objects" bounds every allocated object by the largest signed integer of its index type, 32767 bytes for the 16-bit near space, so a near operand cannot be valid for 65536 bytes and len64k is undefined behaviour. Found by the independent review (finding B2) and reproduced on the downstream toolchain.
items.nextStep: Fixed downstream in 0002 on 2026-09-30 (plan docs/plans/2026-09-30-far-prerequisite-defects.md); carry into the split #320 series.

items.title: Far memset selects the near runtime and loses the destination bank
items.summary: The June 26 4096-byte fill is causally repaired by existing a81874d / patch 0013. Identical retained IR calls near __memset without the patch (4096 physical bytes wrong, checksum 0) and __memset_far with it (all bytes 0x42, checksum 0x2000). The baseline compiler is explicitly reconstructed; no new compiler fix was needed.
items.nextStep: Existing a81874d / 0013 repair revalidated; carry far compiler/ABI and runtime integration with the feature series.

items.title: A fourth far-pointer argument is assigned a 16-bit RS pair
items.summary: In the default far-pointer calling convention (Imag32), CC_MOS offers a far (addrspace 2) pointer only RL1..RL3 and has no fallback of its own. A fourth far-pointer argument falls through to the generic CCIfPtr rule and receives a free 16-bit RSn pair. The machine verifier rejects the resulting 32-bit COPY from a 16-bit register; the downstream release build without the verifier crashes with a segmentation fault. The same holds in plain mosw65816 and under +mos-a16. Found by the independent review of the extracted far series (finding B1) and reproduced on the downstream toolchain.
items.nextStep: Fixed downstream in 0002 on 2026-09-30 (plan docs/plans/2026-09-30-far-prerequisite-defects.md); carry into the split #320 series.

items.title: Combined native-width stack rejects a farblit absolute byte load
items.summary: Patch 0066 repairs the farblit byte-load legalization failure: 0061 eagerly selects an extending far byte load after queuing its generic G_LOAD, and the in-place absolute rewrite leaves that target pseudo on the generic worklist. Build-and-erase removes the queued instruction. The unchanged historical source fails on the preserved baseline and passes with the repair; eight farblit/pressure emulator runs pass.
items.nextStep: 0066 repairs the retained legalization failure. The per-probe Farblit gate now passes on preserved and installed toolchains, including runtime checks. Retain this repair with the far-address/native-width series.

items.title: MOS float-vector arithmetic and scalarization prerequisites
items.summary: Fixed: vector arithmetic reaches scalar float/double libcalls; generic vector prerequisites are backported at the pinned revision.
items.nextStep: Use the reviewed 0050 current-base submission packet; post only when requested.

items.title: HuC6280 block moves into a stack object get the block length as their destination offset
items.summary: Upstream MOSRegisterInfo::eliminateFrameIndex adds the immediate operand that follows a frame index as its displacement. The HuC6280 HuCMemcpy pseudo (src, dst, length, descending) has its length right after the destination frame index, so a block move into a stack object gets length instead of the operand's own offset: a 32-byte constant copied into a local array becomes `tii line,sstk+16,#16; tii line+16,sstk+16,#16`, which writes the first half over the second and leaves bytes 0-15 unset. Silent wrong code on moshuc6280 at -O2 on upstream main 06bc967d2668 (two corpus inputs of the default-mode set change, cardioid and mvscrl). The #321 split commit 'Select native 16-bit compares and fused branches' (#321-11) replaces the heuristic with a per-opcode rule for its own CmpBrAbsImm16 pseudo and fixes this as a side effect; that commit's plan claimed no default-mode effect. Upstream is not fixed.

items.title: Unreserved Imag32 quads over reserved pairs make calls with stack arguments abort
items.summary: llvm-mos#594 (mlund, draft, head 7b80f7e18768) adds RL quads as super-registers of the RS pairs but does not reserve a quad whose pair is reserved. LLVM counts a register unit as reserved only when its root and all of its super-registers are reserved, so the stack pointer RS0 (covered by RL0) stops being reserved at the unit level. Any function that makes a call with stack arguments, such as a variadic call, then aborts in the register coalescer with "LLVM ERROR: Invalid global physical register" (a use of $rs0 without a def during live-range computation), in every MOS CPU mode including default mos6502 code. Reproduced with #594 applied to upstream 06bc967d2668 alone and in the #320 split. Fixed in the split by the commit after #594, which reserves a quad whenever either of its RS pairs is reserved.

items.title: mos-late-opt dereferences a null tracker on an SPC700 LDImm into an imaginary register
items.summary: MOSLateOptimization::combineLdImm selects an A/X/Y tracking slot with a switch over the LDImm destination and then stores through it unconditionally. On SPC700, MOSInstrInfo::getRegClass widens LDImm's destination to Anyi8 to model `mov dp, #imm`, so `$rcN = LDImm imm` is legal, verifier-clean MIR, and the store goes through a null pointer (SIGSEGV). On current upstream main 06bc967d2668 it crashes 31 of the 90 inputs of the series' default-mode set at -mcpu=mosspc700 -O2, 13 of them in-tree CodeGen/MOS tests (fcmp.ll, zp-alloc.ll, light-spill.ll, ...). The fix is our own open upstream PR #584 (restrict the immediate-load folding to GPR destinations), carried downstream as patch 0003 and, since the third round, as its own commit in the #320/#321 split series ahead of #320. Upstream is not fixed until #584 merges, so the status stays confirmed.

items.title: Near addressing folds in upstream llvm-mos leave dangling DBG_VALUEs
items.summary: On upstream llvm-mos 06bc967d2668, a -g near access whose address the MOS legalizer folds into an addressing mode fails -verify-machineinstrs with "Generic virtual register use cannot be undef": a pointer plus a zero-extended byte index (absolute indexed or indirect indexed) at O0 and O2 on mos6502 and mosw65816, and a near global plus a constant at O0. Mechanism: MOSLegalizerInfo::selectAddressingMode (tryAbsoluteAddressing, tryAbsoluteIndexedAddressing, indirect indexed) replaces the access, the G_PTR_ADD that computed its pointer is left with only a debug use, the legalizer erases it, and the generic salvageDebugInfoForDbgValue (llvm/lib/CodeGen/CodeGenCommonISel.cpp) skips a DBG_VALUE it cannot salvage instead of dropping its location, so the DBG_VALUE names an erased register. It is not fixed here. Classification: the trigger is MOS-specific (the MOS legalizer performs addressing-mode folds that erase address arithmetic; other GlobalISel targets fold addresses during selection), and the missing fallback is in generic GlobalISel code. Proposed upstream fix: in llvm-mos, make salvageDebugInfoForDbgValue set an unsalvageable DBG_VALUE to $noreg (setDebugValueUndef), as the IR salvage does, and salvage a G_PTR_ADD with a constant offset as DW_OP_plus_uconst; that generic change also repairs the far sites. A MOS-local alternative is a helper after each fold, like the far-series dropDeadFarAddressDebugUses.

items.title: Native index to imaginary-pair copies lack allocation costs
items.summary: Fixed in the extracted native/far prerequisite series by adding costs for four legal X16/Y16-to-Imag16 copy edges. The two unchanged IR regressions and focused allocation MIR fail on the preserved assertions build and pass after the repair. This is not a claim that the installed downstream compiler contains the change.
items.nextStep: Upheld by the September 30 independent review of the rebased series (patch 9); carry it in the split #321 series.

items.title: Opt-in native-width register classes change default-mode register pressure sets and code
items.summary: Split #321-1 (a359c6b1d73c) adds the single-member classes Ac16, Xc16 and Yc16 for the opt-in 65816 native widths. TableGen derives pressure sets from them: the MOS pressure tables grow from 6 sets to 14 and lose MOSAsmParamRegClass. MachineLICM, MachineSink and the scheduler read those tables in every mode, so default-mode code changes. Against upstream 06bc967d2668 on the split's fixed 90-input set, 18 of 90 mos6502 and 33 of 90 plain mosw65816 results differ, adding +3,478 bytes on mos6502 and +3,202 bytes on mosw65816. Candidate (Phase A, not yet applied to the series or downstream): let GeneratePressureSet = 0 on Ac16/Xc16/Yc16 restores upstream's PressureNameTable/PressureLimitTable exactly and makes default output byte-identical to upstream on all 90 inputs in both modes, in asm and object. At #321-1, +mos-a16 and +mos-a16,+mos-xy16 output also becomes identical to upstream plain mosw65816 (-3,202 bytes). At series head c33eb63d65a3 the change removes 3,515 bytes (mos6502) and 3,379 bytes (mosw65816) of default-mode code, but native output grows by 539 bytes (+mos-a16: 21 inputs larger, 13 smaller) and by 217 bytes (+mos-a16,+mos-xy16: 21 larger, 10 smaller). That growth is unexplained and escalated. Status 2026-09-30: fixed in the #320/#321 split series; downstream 0002 held (escalated), so the record stays confirmed. Ac16, Xc16 and Yc16 set GeneratePressureSet = 0 (split #321-1), so the generated pressure tables equal upstream's; MOSRegisterInfo overrides the pressure-set hooks under +mos-a16 (split #321-8): native classes charge their low byte's sets and, below -O3 (CodeGenOptLevel::Aggressive, read once per subtarget), A16/X16/Y16 sets are appended. Default output at #321-1 is byte-identical to upstream again (90 of 90 inputs, both modes, every level); native bytes at head vs unchanged 321-16: -78/-162 B at -Os, -84/-166 B at -O2, -429/-552 B at -O3; clocks -0.15% at -O2 and -0.18%/-0.17% at -O3. Downstream, the same change grows default-mode code by 13,427 B (+0.58%) over 262 SNES sources at -Os because the downstream computed-carry scheduling (0064/0067) relies on the Ac16/Xc16/Yc16-derived sets; with -mos-carry-sched=off it shrinks default code by 25,290 B. 0002 is unchanged pending the user decision.

items.title: 65816 near indexed addressing carries a wrapping offset into the next bank
items.summary: A signed near offset could be folded into unsigned native indexed addressing, carrying the effective address into DBR+1. Require a no-unsigned-wrap flag or known-bits proof before folding near pointer additions. The isolated DB=$7E regression reads $C3 from $7F before the guard and the expected $5A from $7E afterward.
items.nextStep: Carry the verified near-address wrap guard with the native-width feature series.

items.title: Loop strength reduction loses near-index unsigned-overflow proofs
items.summary: Recover a proven no-unsigned-wrap flag on scalar near byte GEPs immediately after LSR, before its ScalarEvolution facts are invalidated. This repairs a missed optimization; the independent near bank-wrap correctness guard remains required.
items.nextStep: Upstream packet extracted onto 06bc967d2668 and independently reviewed; post with the #321 native-width series when requested.

items.title: opt aborts at startup: near no-wrap recovery pass and its switch share one option name
items.summary: MOSRecoverNearNoWrap registered its legacy pass argument and its -mos-recover-near-nowrap cl::opt under the same string. opt turns every registered legacy pass into a command-line option, so any opt containing the MOS target aborted at startup before reading input; llc and clang were unaffected. The pass is now named mos-near-nowrap-recovery and inserted by ID, in 0002 and in the upstream extraction; the switch keeps its name. The preserved downstream opt aborts on verify.ll and the rebuilt one exits 0; the downstream MOS suites now pass 186 with 3 unsupported and no failures.
items.nextStep: Repaired in 0002 and in the upstream extraction; the upstream fix posts with the near-index recovery patch.

items.title: Broader near-store profitability
items.summary: Patch 0065 completes the measured T3 extensions: indirect store-and-unit arithmetic, indirect call results, zero-extended bytes, and absolute store-and-decrement. The loaded-pointer case retains its smaller native path. This record concerns missed optimizations, not incorrect runtime values.
items.nextStep: Preparation and independent review are complete. Publish when requested under the #321 hold; merge requires #321 and 0063.

items.title: MOS llc crashes during null output when the assembler printer expects a target streamer
items.summary: With -debug-pass=Structure -filetype=null, MOS llc created LLVM's generic MCNullStreamer but MOSAsmPrinter::emitStartOfAsmFile dereferenced its absent target streamer. Registering a MOS null target streamer supplies the expected contract while discarding output. The retained arith.Os.ll crashes with exit 139 on the preserved upstream baseline and completes on the rebuilt candidate; the focused regression and normal object emission pass. The standalone extraction is also validated on upstream 26d7c2c1eebf: 21 null-output failures become successes, 24 ordinary outputs remain byte-identical, and 133 MOS tests pass with one unsupported.
items.nextStep: Obtain independent review of the standalone extraction validated on upstream 26d7c2c1eebf, then submit when requested.

items.title: SPC700 greedy allocation asserts on a copy hint outside the allocation order
items.summary: On upstream main 06bc967d2668 with assertions, -mcpu=mosspc700 -O2 aborts in the Greedy Register Allocator with "Target hint is outside allocation order" on 18 of the 52 corpus IRs of the series' default-mode set (boids, bf-vm, cardioid, mvscrl, ...). MOSRegisterInfo::getRegAllocationHints offers a strong copy hint that the SPC700 allocation order of the class does not contain. Upstream plus #584 still aborts the same way. The #320 split's 1c commit filters a strong hint that is not in the order (added for the empty Imag32 order on non-65816 CPUs); on SPC700 that turns this assertion into "ran out of registers during register allocation" followed by an abort in the Virtual Register Rewriter, so the inputs still fail. Not fixed; root cause in the SPC700 orders not traced.

items.title: Independent Imag8-only rejection hypothesis for i8-to-i1 truncation (0023)
items.summary: The independent claim that an Imag8 source rejects the s8-to-s1 pattern is disproved at vendor pin 8be0546 and saved upstream 742d554: both classes map to Any, and the generated matcher inserts an Ac copy. All 72 compiler runs and 48 selection checks pass. No fix or red baseline is claimed; the unrecovered historical #320 far-pointer observation remains qualified.
items.nextStep: Independent Imag8-only rejection diagnosis disproved. Retain 0023 and its tests with the feature series; the separate historical far-pointer observation still requires its original input and failing compiler.

items.title: O0 65816 vector code exhausts status-register scavenging
items.summary: Fixed: backward scavenger search rechecks target save feasibility before extending the selected spill range. Both original vector tests compile at O0 in a16 and xy16.
items.nextStep: Use the reviewed 0054 current-base submission packet; post only when requested.

items.title: XY16 gallery near decoder fails with a split indirect Y index
items.summary: Fixed locally in 0002: fused near byte/word Y accesses preserve the full index across allocation and REP/SEP insertion. A distinct near-address bank-wrap defect also contributed to the gallery failure and is repaired by an unsigned-wrap proof in address folding. The unchanged 62-work benchmark fails on the reconstructed baseline and fusion-only build, then passes with both repairs (0x5CF0).
items.nextStep: Carry the verified Y-fusion and near-address wrap repairs with the native-width feature series.

items.title: XY16 X preservation saves $p as defined after a call clobbered its flags
items.summary: MOSInsertREPSEP::preserveX decides whether its PH $p reads a defined status register from backward liveness. A scavenger status-register save elsewhere in the loop makes N/Z look live across blocks, so after a JSR that clobbered them preserveX emits PH $p without undef and the machine verifier rejects it. Found as the one candidate-only failure of the near-index proof replay on the extracted upstream series (boids.c, XY16). Given the IR carrying the recovered nuw flags, the prerequisite alone, the candidate and the downstream compiler all fail identically; the same source compiles on the downstream compiler because its earlier passes produce different IR. Only machine verification rejects it; without -verify-machineinstrs the object is emitted.
items.nextStep: Repair preserveX so it saves $p as undefined when no status flag is defined, in 0002 and the #321 prerequisite; red/green on the retained boids.c XY16 IR.

items.title: XY16 width restoration reloads an overwritten X-writer source
items.summary: MOSInsertREPSEP now saves the actual 16-bit X value before narrowing and restores it before a full-width reader, without replaying a mutable or arithmetic writer. The unchanged original XY16 -Os LTO input returns 0xD77B on MAME and bsnes-jg at 1200 frames; the preserved baseline returns 0xD3BD on both. Focused MIR, live-flags/hard-stack runtime cases, and the earlier XY16 in-place-memmove gate pass.
items.nextStep: Local X-preservation repair and original-input red/green on both emulators are complete. Prepare and review the change with #321; retain the separate full-suite opt registration failures.

items.title: SNES soft stack silently overlaps static data (dither -O3 never writes its gate CRC)
items.summary: examples/snes/dither.c built with the SDK driver at -O3 (LTO) never writes corpus_result (0x0000 against 0x80C4) in default mosw65816 and +mos-a16, on bsnes-jg and MAME; -O2 passes. There is no miscompile: the same -O3 instruction stream passes when only the data layout changes. Cause: the SNES platform (platforms/snes/link.ld) puts the soft stack at $2000, growing down into the same low-WRAM region as .bss/.noinit, with no reservation or check. The demo's static data ends at $1FAD (82 B free). At -O3 the pre-link inliner (threshold 250; opt-bisect pass 4016, inline on main) inlines dither_gate_crc and its three unrolled ds_dither calls into main, adding six [66 x i16] locals. main makes 7 indirect calls, so MOSNonReentrant never marks it nonreentrant and its 313 B frame (353 B with +mos-a16) goes on the soft stack at [$1EC7,$2000). The frame overlaps dither_gate_crc.out[478..575] and the whole .noinit static stack. The gate's out[] stores in row 21 overwrite main's spilled row counter and row pointer, and the loop livelocks. Reproduces with upstream llc 06bc967d2668 on the same IR and with an unpatched upstream clang 742d554bf080 full build using this repo's SNES SDK. Placing main's frame on the static stack turns it into a link error (.noinit overflowed by 181 bytes). An earlier instance (rdiff, e3bb5a62, 2026-09-25) was fixed in the demo without a record or guard. Fix location: our SNES platform (a link-time soft-stack reservation and assertion) and/or the differential gate (a soft-SP low-water check); an optional upstream MOSNonReentrant enhancement; not 0002, the #320/#321 patches or generic LLVM. Not fixed; the guard policy is a user decision.
items.nextStep: Choose the guard for SNES soft-stack overflow into static data (a soft-stack low-water check in the differential gate, a link-time soft-stack reservation in the SNES linker scripts, or nonreentrant main per program), then fit or retire dither at -O3. The -O3 code is correct; no compiler change is needed.

items.title: #320 far-address-space compiler and ABI
items.summary: Downstream far-pointer codegen exists; the ABI design note and coherent compiler submission remain.
